/LILIAN

Baltic Exchange Market Report 21 September 2026
Baltic Dry Index: 3399 (29)
Baltic Capesize Index: 5839 (71)
Baltic Panamax Index: 2255 (4)
Baltic Supramax Index: 1771 (4)
Baltic Handysize Index: 993 (5)
CAPESIZE
The Capesize market started the week on a quiet yet positive note, with the BCI 182 5TC gaining a further $638 to $52,953. While activity remained subdued following last Friday's slowdown, the C3 index edged up 8 cents to $43.036. The current C3 assessment window stands at 11 to 21 October, and there are still uncovered West Africa to China cargoes in the market for first half October loading, lending some underlying support to sentiment. In the Pacific, the C5 index rose by $0.29 to $16.865, with activity reported from both miners and operators. The Atlantic remained firm, with talks of tightening tonnage in the Continent/Mediterranean region.

Atlantic
Last weekend, a TBN was taken by Vulcan for 170,000/10 Boca Grande to Qingdao 27/31 October at $50.90.

Asia
Rio Tinto fixed their 170,000/10 Dampier to Qingdao basis 6/8 October at $16.75. Market talk also suggested the Berge Tsurugi (181,403 2012) ETA west Australia 6 October fixed in the high $16s.
PANAMAX
Brokers have reported a firmer start to the week in the Atlantic, driven by an increase in fresh cargo enquiry. Market sources noted that the supply of fixable prompt tonnage off the North Continent is tightening, with early laycans facing greater competition among Charterers, which is lending support to rates. This trend is also providing support to the fronthaul market, despite the P2A posting a slight decline during the day. Owners are reported to be holding firmer on their rate ideas, while those with open tonnage in the Atlantic continue to favour employment within the basin, further underpinning fronthaul levels. Market participants have reported a moderate improvement in activity from both Australia and the North Pacific, with Owners maintaining a firmer stance on rate expectations despite some brokers continuing to highlight a surplus of available tonnage. The YM Centennial (82,659 2026) open CJK 24/25 September was said to have fixed an Australian round at $23,000. Tongli were said to have covered their Gladstone to China 4 October stem, although no other details were reported. Sentiment appears to have improved since last week across both basins, with the P5TC edging up by $35 to close at $20,297.
SUPRAMAX
A very slow start to the week, the BSI was up 4 to 1,771 and the 11TC average was up slightly to $22,389, but despite the FFA market rising this morning, there seemed to be a wait and see attitude. There was a very strong backhaul reported with the Aries Honor (63,743 2025) Nansha 24 September reported fixed via Gulf of Aden to the Mediterranean at $26,000 to T-Bulk and the Xin Wu Xiang Hai (56,797 2012) Ganyu end September fixed a trip West Africa with generals at $22,000, although the Charterer was not revealed. There was also a long period trade announced, the Diana Shipping controlled DSI Polaris (60,404 2018) Mumbai about 25 September fixed to Dai An Ocean Shipping at $18,000 for period minimum 1st May 2028 to maximum 30th June 2028.
HANDYSIZE
The market opened relatively quiet following an active previous week. The BHSI increased by 5 points to 993, while the 7TC average rose by $100 to close at $17,876. The Continent and Mediterranean remained steady, with very limited fixing activity and broadly flat sentiment. The US Gulf and South Atlantic maintained their momentum, supported by a healthy cargo book and a clearing of prompt tonnage, while rates edged above last-done levels. The Pacific market was also broadly flat, with rates hovering around last-done levels.

Atlantic
The Devbulk Kaya (40,527 2012) was fixed for 30,000 mts min/max of urea from Jose Port, Venezuela, to SFDS, Brazil, at $36.50 pmt, although further details were not confirmed. Separately, a large Handysize was heard fixed for a trip from Skaw to the Turkish Black Sea in the high $20,000s, again with limited further details available.

Asia
The HPC Sunrise (35,152 2011) was fixed for loading Silica Sands to Japan at $15,500. Meanwhile, the Daiwan Miracle (34,447 2019), open Lanshan, was fixed by Seanet for a trip via Korea to the west coast of India, with redelivery Port Kelang, at $18,500, although further details were not disclosed.

Market Fundamentals
Chinese Iron Ore Stockpiles

Chinese iron ore stockpiles rose 1.2 Mt to 162.7 Mt in the week to 18 September, according to data from 42 portside locations monitored by Umetal. Inventories stood 25.3 Mt above the same period last year.

Chinese Iron Ore Output

Chinese iron ore output in the year-to-August dropped 8.8% year-on-year to 602.2 Mt, National Bureau of Statistics data show. In August, iron ore production totalled 66.9 Mt, 15.3% lower compared to the same month last year.

Trading Commentary
Cape
The Cape FFA market strengthened into the afternoon. September traded around 49,900–50,000 before firming to 50,250 late, with heavy volume. October opened around 48,750–49,000, pushed to 49,500 during the morning and later reached 49,650. November firmed from 47,000 early to 47,500 late, while December moved from around 44,250 to 44,600. Q4 26 traded around 46,750–47,000 for much of the session before strengthening to 47,250 late. Q1 27 was active around 32,400–32,550 before pushing to 33,000 and finishing around 32,800. Q2 27 firmed from 36,500 to 36,750, while Cal 27 moved from 34,000 to 34,300. Overall, the market finished with a firmer tone and strong late activity across the curve.

PMX
PMX was firm today, with strength building across the front end. September traded 21,400 before easing slightly to 21,350 late. October opened around 22,500, pushed through 22,800–23,000 during the day and finished firmer around 23,150–23,200. November moved from 22,850 early to 23,000–23,100 through most of the day before reaching 23,350 late. December traded from 21,950–22,000 early, firmed to 22,150 and later printed 22,300. Q4 26 started around 22,350, traded mostly 22,600–22,700 midday and strengthened to 22,800–22,850 late. Q1 27 moved from 18,450 early to 18,700 later. Q2 27 traded 19,400–19,600, while Cal 27 remained around 18,400–18,500. Overall, the session finished with a firmer tone across the curve.

SMX + HANDY
SMX was supported today, with most interest in October and Q4. October traded 21,800 early, moved up to 21,950 through the morning and held mostly 21,850–21,900 through midday before firming to 22,000 late.
